ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in the Amazon basin changed by +0.189 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.124 to +0.256), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.467 °C.

cautions: The confidence interval is wide compared with the trend, so the size of the change is uncertain.
ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in the Amazon basin changed by +0.063 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.008 to +0.119), which is statistically significant (p = 0.02). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.155 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in the Amazon basin shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.44): the estimate is +0.07 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.10 to +0.24). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in the Amazon basin shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.49): the estimate is +0.0024 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0049 to +0.0096). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in the Amazon basin shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.60): the estimate is −0.004 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.019 to +0.010). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
